newsitem.title: USA: Taiwan, trade hurt ties with U.S. - China's Qian.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, trade hurt ties with U.S. - China's Qian.

text.p: Two hurdles to improved Sino-U.S. relations lie in the nations' differences over Taiwan and the recurring issue of China's trade status, Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen said on Friday.
"Among all these troubles, the question of Taiwan has certainly been most disruptive and most damaging to China-U.S. relations," Qian told the Chicago Council on Foreign Relations.
Qian reiterated China's strong desire for the reunification of Taiwan with the mainland and repeated that China had not "ruled out the use of force" to accomplish it.

"The ups and downs in recent years show clearly that if the Taiwan question is handled properly, China-U.S. relations will progress smoothly. If not, they will suffer setbacks or even serious retrogression," he said.
"We attach importance to the renewed pledge of American leaders thay that will pursue a 'one China' policy," Qian said.

On the issue of economic and trade ties, Qian said the annual U.S. review of China's most-favored-nation trade status "makes our economic and trade ties unstable (and) also disrupts the overall relationship." He said he hoped for a "permanent solution" to the issue.

Qian responded to a question about the future role of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum by noting that China was a member of APEC but remained outside the World Trade Organization (WTO).

"If China is not a member of the World Trade Organization, it will have a lot of difficulty implementing the program of APEC. Therefore, China's approach is that all APEC members should receive support to become members of the WTO," Qian responded through an interpreter.
